target_window.policy: Relative harvest observations may validate interannual risk and climate response. They are not absolute kg_per_ha labels unless an independently documented sowing-rate and footprint bridge exists.

decision_summary.new_open_in_period_relative_source: Hao et al. eastern China harvest grades, 801-1910; article and grading supplement acquired and hashed, but the annual machine-readable series is available only from the authors on request.
decision_summary.new_open_in_period_absolute_source_reaso: No non-English 1100-1500 source with both a mappable footprint and absolute annual yield units was found in the reviewed repositories. This is a research blocker, not permission to impute labels.

sources.title: Patterns in data of extreme droughts/floods and harvest grades derived from historical documents in eastern China during 801-1910
sources.citation: Hao, Z., Wu, M., Zheng, J., Chen, J., Zhang, X., and Luo, S. (2020), Climate of the Past 16, 101-116

local_files.derivation: deterministic pypdf text extraction from the article PDF
publisher full-text XML; confirms data-availability statement and contains no annual series

historical_semantics.spatial_resolution: station chronologies each covering approximately 20 counties; subregions are broad envelopes, not EU5-equivalent historical polygons

grade_scale.1: very poor, below 40 percent of normal harvest

historical_semantics.urbanization_or_trade_hub: regional documentary series; not a city or port target

period_direction_check.target_window_relevant_note: The 1100-1250 interval is summarized as generally bumper; 1251-1500 includes the transition to a generally poor regime. This is a climate/harvest-risk validation signal only.

availability_and_limitations.availability_statement: The article states that all data are available from the corresponding authors on request; the open supplement contains grading criteria but not the annual series.
availability_and_limitations.selection_bias: Historical sources preferentially record abnormal years; the paper explicitly documents missing/normal-year bias.
availability_and_limitations.shared_source_family: official histories, chronicles, gazetteers and related documentary compilations; not independent from other Chinese documentary chronologies
can_be_used_for: uncertainty scenario stress tests after raw annual data are obtained

sources.title: Relationships between temperature change and grain harvest fluctuations in China from 210 BC to 1910 AD
sources.citation: Yin, J., Su, Y., and Fang, X. (2015), Quaternary International 355, 153-163

historical_semantics.method: textual descriptions converted to ordinal harvest levels and aggregated at decadal resolution

availability_and_limitations.reason: The reviewed public landing page exposes the publication but not a downloadable series; values shown in figures are not digitized here.
availability_and_limitations.boundary: broad national/eastern China envelope; insufficient for EU5 footprint targets
availability_and_limitations.technology_and_crop_system_drift: Long period includes changing borders, crop varieties, agricultural area and management; not a stationary 1337 target
can_be_used_for: qualitative or digitized decadal harvest-risk validation after independent digitization

sources.title: Reassessing long-term drought risk and societal impacts in Shenyang, Liaoning Province, north-east China (1200-2015)
sources.citation: Tang, L., Macdonald, N., Sangster, H., Chiverrell, R., and Gaulton, R. (2020), Climate of the Past 16, 1917-1935

historical_semantics.observation_type: historical drought severity and agricultural impact chronology
historical_semantics.relative_harvest_signal: The source inventory states that Liaoning drought ratings for 12 key cities (including Shenyang) from 352-1948 were based on grain-yield reduction rates.
historical_semantics.city_or_trade_hub: Shenyang is a city selector; not a surrounding rural capacity target

availability_and_limitations.available_material: The open article, supplement and Table 1 inventory identify the archival source and its semantics; the annual 352-1948 drought-rating table is not included in the downloaded assets.
availability_and_limitations.boundary: The source discusses Shenyang and Liaoning administrative areas; the EU5 crosswalk uses the named Shenyang location only as a local climate/harvest-risk validation point.
availability_and_limitations.shared_source_family: Chinese documentary and local-record compilations; do not count as independent from Hao/Yin documentary harvest sources.
can_be_used_for: relative drought-to-yield-reduction direction after raw rating data are obtained

sources.title: Rain-fed agriculture thrived despite climate degradation in the pre-Hispanic arid Andes
sources.citation: Cruz, P., Winkel, T., Ledru, M.-P., Bernard, C., Egan, N., Swingedouw, D., and Joffre, R. (2017), Science Advances 3, e1701740

historical_semantics.geography: Intersalar region, southern Bolivian Altiplano; study sites and croplands around the Uyuni/Lipez area
historical_semantics.yield_semantics: The range is measured in present-day carefully hand-farmed mountain-slope fields; the paper argues practices remained broadly unchanged and uses it as a framework for inferring ancient production, not as direct archaeological annual yield.
historical_semantics.archaeological_date_evidence: 16 radiocarbon dates 1200-1450 CE; quinoa grains in Jirira Vinto granaries dated 1324-1440 CE
historical_semantics.rotation: two-year rain-fed crop/fallow rotation; effective annualized cropped fraction is approximately one half
historical_semantics.climate_constraints: annual rainfall below 350 mm, high-altitude frost and wind; quinoa survives lower temperatures than potato

availability_and_limitations.modern_analogue_bridge: The authors explicitly rely on continuity of Andean agricultural practices to infer ancient techniques; this is a physical plausibility range, not an observed medieval harvest panel.
availability_and_limitations.boundary: No machine-readable study polygon is supplied in the downloaded paper; the crosswalk retains a broad transparent coordinate selector only.
can_be_used_for: rain-fed high-altitude crop/fallow and storage-risk validation
testing that cold arid locations are not forced to zero when a historically documented staple is feasible
cannot_be_used_for: annual risk calibration without additional time series

sources.title: Inequality in agricultural production and health of Hohokam era irrigation farmers, CE 1200 to 1400

historical_semantics.observation_type: archaeological irrigation and bioarchaeological production/health comparison

sources.reason: Six Lower Salt River irrigation villages provide a relevant pre-1337 hydraulic/agricultural contrast, but the publication does not provide annual yield labels or a population-capacity interval for the surrounding EU5-equivalent footprint.

remaining_blockers: Obtain Hao annual grade series from the authors or a licensed archive if annual risk scoring is required.
Digitize or obtain the Yin decadal series only for relative held-out validation; do not use it as an absolute target.
Find or document the absence of a non-English 1100-1500 source with absolute yield units and an exact mappable footprint.
